symptom: ako/mxcli#1793: for a self-referencing Reference M.Order_Parent (M.Order to M.Order), `retrieve $P from $Order/M.Order_Parent; $n = count $P;` passed `check -p --references` and exec ("Created microflow"), then mx check failed CE0013 "Input variable 'P' must be of type 'List'." The full build typed $P `List of M.Order` unless an object use followed; the splice path (#1777) already typed it M.Order.
cause: Three answers to 'which end does this association retrieve start from': addRetrieveAction asked only 'is the start the child (TO) entity', which a self-reference always is, so it read as a reverse traversal; flowBuilder.associationRetrieveType (#1777) special-cased the self-reference as the FROM end; check's associationRetrieveShape returned known=false for from == to and took the nearest generalization link otherwise; validateFlowBody's forwardReferenceTarget kept a self-association a list. And the check judged only a list used as an object, never one object used as a list, so even a forward Reference `count` (CE0013) was silent.
file: mdl/executor/validate_retrieve_association_list.go (associationRetrieveEnd, associationRetrieveShape, listActivityInput, the MDL-RETRIEVE01 half of validateAssociationRetrieveListUse), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go (associationRetrieveEndFrom, addRetrieveAction, associationRetrieveType), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_validate.go (forwardReferenceTarget), mdl/executor/validate_flow_member_refs.go (scriptGeneralizationChain)
fix: One rule, associationRetrieveEnd(isFrom, isTo, self): both ends + self-reference = FROM, both ends of two different entities = ambiguous (the build keeps its old TO reading, the splice and the check stay silent), else the end it is. The build, the splice, check --references and validateFlowBody all ask it. check --references now reports MDL-RETRIEVE01 for the one object a Reference followed from its FROM end binds (self-reference or not) taken by an aggregate (CE0013), a list operation but range (CE0097), a loop (CE0100) or a list parameter (CE0117); exec's pre-flight refuses the same. A one-to-one from its TO end is not judged (the build rewrites a list use into a database retrieve). The start's chain is read through the script's declarations first, so a specialization the script creates counts.
test: cmd_microflows_builder_retrieve_self_reference_test.go (TestBuildFlowGraph_SelfReferenceIsFollowedFromItsFromEnd, TestBuildFlowGraph_AssociationDirectionControls, TestAssociationRetrieveType_AgreesWithTheFullBuild); validate_retrieve_self_reference_test.go (TestAssociationRetrieveObjectUsedAsList: 11 refused shapes, 10 controls; _ScriptDeclaredSpecialization; SelfReferenceSetUsedAsObject; TestCheckSetOnSelfReferenceObject). mdl-examples/bug-tests/1793-self-reference-retrieve-is-the-object.mdl. Control: the fix's source files reverted to main -> $P typed List of Sample.Node, the owner-Both self-reference expanded to a DatabaseRetrieveSource, the check returns no error for every list use. Knock-on: bug-tests 1323 (item 2, set over a self-reference Reference) and 1100 (SUB_LoopAssoc looped over a FROM-end Reference: exec as written is CE0100 on 11.13.0) held shapes the rule now refuses; both rewritten to the measured-valid shape.
insight: Measure every activity kind before refusing, not one: over the same object on 11.13.0 every aggregate is CE0013, every list operation CE0097 EXCEPT range (Microflows$ListRange, 0 errors), a loop CE0100, a list parameter CE0117, and add/remove/clear/set (Change list) 0 errors — mx check does not type a Change list's variable or a range's. That last gap is why #1323's bug-test claimed 'Mendix types a self-association retrieve as a list': its `set` was written as Change list Replace and passed; mx check's CE0100 text names the variable's type outright ("'P' is of type M.Order"), which is the measurement to trust. When a fix adds a helper that answers a question another site answers too, grep for every site (here four) and route them through one function with a test that the two builder paths agree.
